one_month_reasoning: Lumentum's fiscal Q1 FY27 ended in late September; last year it reported fiscal Q1 on Nov 4 (8-K 2025-11-04), so the Q1 FY27 print most likely lands just after the 2026-11-01 window and is not counted. Inside the window: late-October hyperscaler earnings and capex guidance (Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon), which drive AI-optics sentiment and lately have mostly been supportive, plus NVIDIA-related newsflow. Against that, the stock closed within 0.6% of its 52-week high after a +533% year, and insiders are selling almost daily (a string of Form 144s and Form 4s in Sept-Oct 2026, e.g. an officer's 24,542-share Form 144 on 2026-10-01). Short-horizon momentum and reversal roughly offset, so I use a symmetric lognormal centred on $1085 with a one-month log-sd of about 0.22, a little below 97%/3.5 = 28% because no earnings fall in the window.

fair_value.method: Forward P/E as of Oct 2027. My NTM EPS then (FQ2 FY28 to FQ1 FY29) is about $32, built by extending the Q1 FY27 guide ($4.05-4.35) at slowing sequential growth. At 30x that gives ~$960, and FY28 EPS of about $29.5 at 35x gives ~$1,030. Blended FV is ~$1,000, roughly flat against today's $1,085.

bear.story: AI capex digestion or a hyperscaler pause in 2027, combined with competitors' and Chinese transceiver/EML capacity catching up, cuts pricing and margins. Customer A or B moves share. EPS plateaus near $20 and the multiple derates to ~22x, so the stock gives back most of the 2026 rally, as optical stocks have done in past cycle tops.

base.story: Lumentum executes the guided ramp, revenue passes ~$1.6-1.8B a quarter by mid-2027, and margins hold ~40%. Earnings roughly double, but the multiple compresses from ~52x to ~30-35x forward, so the price stays roughly flat.

bull.story: Capacity adds keep the ramp near +20% Q/Q, scale-out CPO and ELS lasers ship from 2H CY2027, OCS keeps growing, and NTM EPS reaches $45-50 by late 2027 on a sustained ~40x multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $600 is ~19x my Oct-2027 NTM EPS and ~45% below today. Ordinary volatility (~65-95%/yr) could get there, but only together with a derating that implies the market expects EPS to stall. That would most likely mean sequential guidance cuts, lost share at Customer A/B, or an AI capex pullback, not just noise. It is also below NVIDIA's $695 preferred entry price.

reasoning: Primary-document lane. The Q4 FY26 8-K release shows revenue up 109% Y/Y to $1.006B, non-GAAP GM 50.4%, op margin 36.6%, and EPS $3.23. Q1 FY27 guidance is $1.25B at the midpoint (+24% Q/Q), op margin ~40%, and EPS $4.20, reaching the target model a quarter early. The 10-K adds detail the recaps skip. Customer A grew to 26.6% of revenue and Customer B is 15.0%. NVIDIA bought $2.0B of 1:1 convertible preferred at $695.31 in March 2026. Exchanges of $1.12B of converts for 10.6M shares created the $7.8B non-cash loss. $1.55B of convertible principal is still outstanding (2032 notes convert at $187.77). FY26 capex was $451M against operating cash flow of $751M. Demand exceeds supply, and the company is allocating product. EDGAR also shows near-daily insider Form 144/Form 4 filings in Sept-Oct 2026. To value it, I extend the guide at fading sequential growth and get FY27 EPS of ~$21 and Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$32. At 30-35x that gives ~$1,000, roughly today's price: strong earnings growth offset by multiple compression from ~52x FY27. So my median is a little below spot (~$1,050). Spread: realized vol is 97%. I use a forward log-sd of ~0.66 because some of the past move was a one-off rerating. The left tail is fat because AI optical names have a history of 60-75% cycle drawdowns, and the right tail stays open for a sustained shortage plus CPO. Research limits: the Q4 deck PDF was image-only and could not be read. Full transcripts were paywalled, so I used a call summary. Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable (plan limits), so there is no fresh consensus. Analyst figures I cite are from earlier in 2026 and serve only as anchors.
